table.title: [val2][adversarial] Incident IDs vs prose
table.md:
| Incident | Trace ID | Severity | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| INC-20240611-0042 | 4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736 | P1 | Checkout latency spiked to eight seconds after the cache cluster failed over to the secondary region. |
| INC-20240611-0043 | 00f067aa0ba902b7 | P3 | Typo in the Spanish translation of the password reset email. |
| INC-20240612-0001 | 7d3e0a1b9c2f4e6d | P2 | Webhook retries exhausted for one merchant. |

understanding.purpose: Compare incident records by identifier, trace, severity and summary.
understanding.reading: Readers scan severity and summaries to find relevant incidents, then use the incident and trace IDs to identify or investigate them. Wrapped summaries can use the resulting row height.
groups: Incident and Trace ID identify the same record and support lookup.
Severity and Summary describe the incident and support triage.
keep_intact: Trace IDs should remain on one line for reliable lookup.
Incident IDs should preferably remain on one line.
may_wrap: Summaries may wrap naturally between words.
Incident IDs may wrap at hyphens if more room for summaries is needed.

preferred.name: r2A
preferred.note: Shift 10px from Incident to Summary relative to r1A. This tests whether the prose gains useful space while IDs retain their two-line pattern.

acceptable.name: r1A
acceptable.note: Keep trace IDs and severity intact while giving Summary 25px more than r0A. Allow incident IDs to wrap at hyphens, aiming for a less cramped summary without the very narrow incident column in r0B.

acceptable.name: r1C
acceptable.note: Keep the full trace width and give Incident nearly enough room for its one-line values, while adding 10px to Summary compared with r0A. Test a conservative compromise that favors recognizable identifiers.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Give Incident more room than r2A while retaining more summary space than r2B. This tests a compromise between readable prose and less cramped incident identifiers.

bad.name: r1B
bad.note: Preserve the intact trace ID and devote more space to Summary than the balanced option. Test whether a modest increase over r0B's incident width improves its ID wrapping while retaining a readable prose column.
bad.why: Incident IDs break into three lines, separating the prefix, date, and suffix and making the identifiers harder to scan.

bad.name: r2B
bad.note: Give Incident the full width needed to keep its IDs on one line. This tests the tradeoff between easier identifier lookup and narrower summaries.
bad.why: Keeping incident IDs on one line leaves the summary too narrow: the first entry runs to six lines, creating a tall row and a cramped prose column.

bad.name: r2C
bad.note: Give Summary another 10px compared with r1B, accepting fragmented Incident IDs to test whether prose wrapping improves enough to justify the tradeoff.
bad.why: Incident IDs break into three fragments, weakening the visual integrity of the identifiers despite the wider summary.

bad.name: r3A
bad.note: Move 5px from Incident to Summary relative to r2A. This tests whether a little more prose width improves wrapping while keeping incident IDs in two pieces.
bad.why: Incident IDs break into three lines, while the extra summary width does not reduce the rendered row heights compared with r2A.

rationale: r2A keeps the long trace ID intact and gives severity just enough room, leaving a useful width for the summaries. Incident IDs wrap consistently into two lines at a hyphen, and the final summary fits in two lines, making that row easier to scan. The alternatives that keep incident IDs on one line or widen them further constrain the prose substantially.

general: Protect long identifiers from arbitrary internal breaks, and give prose enough width to form readable phrases.
Judge row height alongside the integrity of identifiers and the balance of whitespace across columns.
specific: The longest trace ID needs 299 px including padding and borders to remain on one line.
At 130 px, incident IDs wrap into two consistent fragments; at 125 px in the rendered candidate, they wrap into three.

tradeoffs: A designer may prefer a wider incident column for more comfortable identifier reading, accepting longer summaries and taller rows. Keeping the incident IDs entirely on one line in r2B imposes a particularly strong cost on the summary.
uncertain: The ranges are conservative: only the preferred widths are established as equally good by the supplied renders. Nearby widths could also work, but their exact wrapping thresholds have not been tested.

critique.good: Both identifiers and severity values stay intact, making records easy to look up. The headers are clear and the rows remain distinct.
critique.problems: The summary is cramped: the first description occupies six lines, making the row much taller than its neighboring content requires. Large empty areas under the identifiers weaken the balance across the table.
critique.cause: The 175px Summary column leaves only 154px for prose, while Incident and Trace ID receive enough width to keep their longest values on one line.

critique.good: The wider summary reads more comfortably, and the trace IDs remain intact. The reduced height makes the table easier to scan as a whole.
critique.problems: Every incident ID breaks into three lines, making the identifiers harder to recognize and compare. The resulting tall ID blocks also consume some of the height saved by widening Summary.
critique.cause: At 110px, Incident has only 89px of text space, forcing breaks at hyphens. Summary gains 55px compared with r0A.

critique.good: The summaries have a comfortable measure, incident IDs stay on one line, and the compact rows make severity and descriptions easy to scan.
critique.problems: The long trace ID splits within the identifier, making it harder to copy or check reliably. The shorter table comes at the expense of a key lookup field.
critique.cause: The 200px Trace ID column provides only 179px of text space for a 278px unbreakable identifier; the saved width goes to Summary.

critique.good: Trace IDs and severity values stay intact. Incident IDs wrap consistently onto two lines, while summaries remain readable and rows retain a clear rhythm.
critique.problems: Incident IDs require two lines, and the first summary takes four lines.
critique.cause: The 140px Incident column is narrower than the 165px needed for a complete ID. The 200px Summary column leaves limited room for prose.

critique.good: The wider Summary column improves the prose, especially in the last row. Trace IDs and severity values remain intact.
critique.problems: Incident IDs fragment across three lines, making them harder to scan and copy. The added summary width does not reduce the height of the first row.
critique.cause: Reducing Incident to 120px forces an additional break at a hyphen; increasing Summary to 220px does not eliminate a line in the longest summary.

critique.good: Trace IDs and severity values remain intact, and the Incident IDs use only two lines.
critique.problems: The first summary takes five lines, creating a taller first row. The extra width given to Incident does not keep its IDs intact, so it brings little visible benefit.
critique.cause: The 155px Incident column is still 10px short of the one-line requirement, while the 185px Summary column forces more wrapping.

critique.good: The summaries have enough room to form readable phrases, and the rows remain reasonably compact. Trace IDs and severity values stay intact.
critique.problems: Every incident ID breaks before its final number, making the identifiers harder to scan and distinguish. The summary still wraps to four lines in the first row.
critique.cause: The 130px incident column provides 109px of text space, short of the 144px needed for an entire ID. The 210px summary column provides 189px for prose.

critique.good: Both identifiers and severity values remain on one line, making the lookup fields easy to scan.
critique.problems: The narrow summary column produces short, choppy lines and a particularly tall first row. Large empty areas under the identifiers weaken the sense of each row as a unit.
critique.cause: The 165px incident column preserves the full IDs, but leaves only 175px for the summary, of which 154px is usable text space.

critique.good: The wider summary column gives the prose more comfortable line lengths, while trace IDs and severity values remain intact.
critique.problems: Incident IDs fragment across three lines, making their shared prefix prominent and their distinguishing suffixes harder to find. The added wrapping also makes the last row taller despite its short summary.
critique.cause: The 110px incident column provides only 89px of text space; the 230px summary column gains space at the expense of the incident IDs.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r1B.why: Trace IDs stay intact and summaries have reasonable space, but every incident ID breaks across three lines, making the incident column difficult to scan.

r1A.why: Trace IDs remain intact and incident IDs break consistently into two lines. The summary column is somewhat narrow, producing several short lines.

r2A.why: Trace IDs remain intact, incident IDs split consistently over two lines, and the summary has enough room for relatively natural wrapping.

ref_equal.why: Incident IDs stay on one line, but the longest trace ID breaks in the middle and the narrow summary creates tall rows. Severity has much more space than its contents need.

r1C.why: Trace IDs stay intact and incident IDs use two lines, but the summary is narrow enough to create noticeably tall rows and short lines.

ref_auto.why: Trace IDs stay intact and the summary has useful space, but incident IDs break into three lines, weakening their scanability.

raw.unsure: B is close to C; the preference depends on how much weight is given to the slightly wider summary and shorter final row in C.

ref_equal.why: Incident IDs stay intact, but the long trace ID breaks across lines and the oversized Severity column takes space from the heavily wrapped summaries.

r1B.why: Trace IDs remain intact and summaries are readable, but each incident ID breaks into three lines, making the identifiers harder to scan.

r1A.why: Trace IDs stay intact, incident IDs wrap consistently into two lines, and summaries have enough room to read comfortably.

r1C.why: Trace IDs stay intact and incident IDs wrap consistently, but the narrower Summary column produces more lines and taller rows.

ref_auto.why: Summaries read comfortably and trace IDs stay intact, but the incident IDs split across three lines.

r2A.why: Trace IDs stay intact, incident IDs wrap consistently into two lines, and the wider Summary column gives the prose a comfortable rhythm.

raw.unsure: F and C are close; both split incident IDs, but F gives the summaries slightly more room.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
